quests.instruction: You put on a long-sleeved shirt. Which two body parts slide into the sleeves?
quests.hint: Sleeves are made to fit between your shoulders and your hands.
quests.explanation: Sleeves cover your arms, which stretch from your shoulders to your hands. Long sleeves keep them warm.
quests.funFact: Stretch your arms out wide, and the distance from fingertip to fingertip is close to your height.

quests.instruction: You pull on your trousers, one side at a time. Which body parts slide inside?
quests.hint: There is one for each side, and each has a knee in the middle.
quests.explanation: Trousers cover your legs, from your hips down toward your feet. That is why they have two tubes, one for each leg.
quests.funFact: Your leg bones keep growing until you are a teenager.

quests.instruction: A friend gives you a bead necklace. Which part of your body does it hang around?
quests.hint: It is a narrow part, right under your head.
quests.explanation: A necklace hangs around your neck, the narrow part that joins your head to your shoulders.
quests.funFact: Air and food both pass through your neck on their way down into your body.

quests.instruction: Your hair and your face are both parts of which body part?
quests.hint: It sits at the very top of your body, above your neck.
quests.explanation: Your head holds your face, your hair, and the skull that protects your brain.
quests.funFact: A baby's skull has soft gaps between its bones, and the gaps close as the baby grows.

quests.instruction: Shoulder at the top, elbow in the middle, hand at the end. Which body part has all three?
quests.hint: You use them to hug, carry, and reach.
quests.explanation: An arm runs from the shoulder, past the elbow, down to the hand.
quests.funFact: Each arm, counting the hand, has 30 bones.

quests.instruction: Your belly button is found on which part of your body?
quests.hint: It is the soft front part, below your ribs.
quests.explanation: Your belly button is on your tummy. It is a small scar from the cord that brought you food before you were born.
quests.funFact: Some belly buttons poke out and some tuck in. Both kinds are completely normal.

quests.instruction: Make a wish, then blow out the candles on your birthday cake. Which part does the blowing?
quests.hint: You make a small, round shape with it when you whistle.
quests.explanation: You blow air out through your mouth, shaping your lips into a small circle to send out a steady puff.
quests.funFact: The air you blow out comes from your lungs. Your mouth only shapes it.

quests.instruction: Something smells awful! Which part do you pinch closed with two fingers?
quests.hint: It is in the middle of your face and has two openings.
quests.explanation: Pinching your nose blocks the smell from coming in through your nostrils.
quests.funFact: Your two nostrils take turns: one usually lets in more air than the other, and they swap during the day.

quests.instruction: Clap, clap, clap! Which body parts smack together to make the sound?
quests.hint: They are at the ends of your arms.
quests.explanation: You clap with your hands, bringing your palms together quickly so the air between them makes a pop.
quests.funFact: About one person in ten is left-handed.

quests.instruction: Which parts come loose and fall out around age six or seven, while bigger ones grow in to replace them?
quests.hint: You might wiggle a loose one with your tongue.
quests.explanation: Children lose their baby teeth, usually starting around age six, and larger adult teeth grow in their place.
quests.funFact: Adult teeth are meant to last for life, so you only get one more set.

quests.instruction: As people get older, which part of their head often turns gray or white?
quests.hint: It grows out of your scalp.
quests.explanation: Hair gets its color from a natural pigment. Over time, hair makes less of it, so it can turn gray or white.
quests.funFact: Your hair is made of a tough material that is also found in fingernails.

quests.instruction: You cannot see it in the mirror unless you turn around. Which wide part of your body is behind you?
quests.hint: The tag on a shirt is usually sewn near the top of it, on the inside.
quests.explanation: Your back is on the rear side of your body, so you need a second mirror or a helper to see it.
quests.funFact: Seen from the side, your spine curves gently, a bit like a soft letter S.

quests.instruction: Which body parts are closed when you are fast asleep?
quests.hint: You cannot see anything while they are shut.
quests.explanation: When you sleep, your eyelids close over your eyes, which rests them and keeps them moist.
quests.funFact: While you dream, your eyes often move around under your closed eyelids.

quests.instruction: You lift your heels off the floor to reach a high shelf. Which parts of your feet are still pressed on the floor?
quests.hint: They are at the front of your feet.
quests.explanation: When you rise up, your heels lift and your weight moves to the front of your feet, onto your toes.
quests.funFact: Your toes grip the floor a little to help you stay balanced.

quests.instruction: You walk across the room with a book balanced on top of you. Which part is holding it up?
quests.hint: It is the highest part of your body.
quests.explanation: A light book can balance on your head while your neck and back keep you standing straight.
quests.funFact: The muscles in your neck work all day to keep your head balanced on top of your spine.

quests.instruction: I live inside your shoes. I have a heel at the back and five toes at the front. What am I?
quests.hint: You stand on me.
quests.explanation: Feet have a heel at the back and five toes at the front. They hold your weight so you can stand.
quests.funFact: Your feet have thousands of tiny sweat glands.

quests.instruction: I am a bendy muscle inside your mouth. I wiggle to help you say words like "la la la." What am I?
quests.hint: You can curl me and stick me out.
quests.explanation: Your tongue moves to shape sounds, which is how you say words such as "la" and "ta."
quests.funFact: Your tongue is not one muscle but several muscles working together.

quests.instruction: I sit between your neck and your arm. I rise when you shrug and drop when you relax. What am I?
quests.hint: You can roll me in big circles, front to back.
quests.explanation: Shoulders lift when you shrug and drop when you relax. They link your arms to the rest of your body.
quests.funFact: Your collarbone runs along the top of your chest and connects to your shoulder.

quests.instruction: Touch your shoulder, then trace all the way down your arm. Which of these do you reach last?
quests.hint: It is the very end of your arm.
quests.explanation: Going down your arm, you pass the shoulder, then the elbow, and finish at the fingers.
quests.funFact: Fingers have no muscles inside them. Strings called tendons pull them, from muscles in your hand and forearm.

quests.instruction: Your thigh is above it and your shin is below it. Which part is it?
quests.hint: It bends when you climb stairs.
quests.explanation: The thigh bone above and the shin bone below meet at the knee, a joint that bends.
quests.funFact: Babies do not have hard kneecaps yet. They start out as soft cartilage that turns to bone by about age three to five.

quests.instruction: Climb up your body from your knees. Which of these do you reach last before your head?
quests.hint: It sits on top of your chest and holds your head.
quests.explanation: Going up from your knees, you pass your tummy, then your chest, and finally your neck, which connects to your head.
quests.funFact: Most people can turn their head far enough to look almost directly over each shoulder.

quests.instruction: Your eyes spot a ball flying toward you. Which part moves to catch it?
quests.hint: They grip and hold things.
quests.explanation: Your eyes tell your brain where the ball is, and your hands move to catch it. Eyes and hands work as a team.
quests.funFact: Eye and hand teamwork gets better with practice, which is why players improve the more they play.

quests.instruction: You chew a bite of apple. Which part pushes the chewed food to the back of your mouth so you can swallow?
quests.hint: It is soft and moves around inside your mouth.
quests.explanation: The tongue pushes chewed food toward the back of your mouth, where swallowing begins.
quests.funFact: When you swallow, a small flap closes off your windpipe so the food goes down the right way.

quests.instruction: Your eyes sit in the middle of your face. Which parts sit on the sides of your head, about level with your eyes?
quests.hint: You can feel their soft, curved edges with your fingers.
quests.explanation: Ears are on each side of your head, roughly in line with your eyes.
quests.funFact: Your ears also help you balance. A part deep inside tells your brain when your head tilts.

quests.instruction: On a piggyback ride, your friend climbs onto which part of your body?
quests.hint: It faces away from the direction you are looking.
quests.explanation: Piggyback riders sit against your back, held up by your arms hooked under their legs.
quests.funFact: Your spine has gentle curves that act like a spring, which helps you absorb bumps when you walk and run.

quests.instruction: A big belly laugh makes which part of your body bounce?
quests.hint: It is below your chest, at the front.
quests.explanation: A big laugh squeezes the muscles of your tummy, which is why it can shake and even ache afterward.
quests.funFact: Laughing works your tummy muscles, a little like a gentle exercise.

quests.instruction: Which part of your body can be braided, tied in a ponytail, or clipped back?
quests.hint: You can cut it without it hurting.
quests.explanation: Hair is long and bendy, so it can be braided, tied, or clipped. Cutting it does not hurt because the part you see is not alive.
quests.funFact: Most people lose about 50 to 100 hairs a day, and new ones grow in to replace them.

quests.instruction: Eyes, nose, and mouth are all found on which part of your head?
quests.hint: It is the front of your head.
quests.explanation: The face is the front of your head. It holds your eyes, nose, and mouth.
quests.funFact: Your face has 14 bones.

quests.instruction: You take a big, deep breath. Which part of your upper body gets bigger?
quests.hint: Your ribs are inside it.
quests.explanation: When you breathe in, your ribs move up and out, and your chest gets a little bigger.
quests.funFact: Children breathe about 20 times every minute while resting.

quests.instruction: Stand beside a friend and compare. Which of these is longer on most children?
quests.hint: They carry your whole body when you walk.
quests.explanation: Legs are longer than arms, which suits their job of carrying your body.
quests.funFact: By the time you are a grown-up, your legs will make up about half of your height.
